headline: St. Olavsleden is a month out, yet no loaded or back-to-back durability work has surfaced in the recent block.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic picture is settled and favourable — the lower easy-run HR now holds across a full block of comparable efforts, so treat that adaptation as banked rather than provisional. Volume is essentially flat versus the prior block, which reads as consolidation on top of a genuine ramp, not regression. Strength has doubled its session count over the previous four weeks, so the raised volume you were watching has held rather than reverting — that's the more notable stability story this week than the running numbers.

The gap worth naming is specificity. You have a 580 km self-supported trail crossing with a 6-8 kg pack in a month, and the recent running has been unloaded, single-day, and on modest elevation. Aerobic efficiency and strength are both trending the right way, but pack-carrying and consecutive-day time-on-feet remain the least-rehearsed qualities relative to what the route will actually demand. That's a training-design observation, not a fitness concern — your base and threshold are clearly intact.
watch_items: Whether consecutive-day or pack-loaded efforts start entering the block, given the route's self-supported multi-day profile.
Whether elevation and time-on-feet per session increase, since the crossing involves sustained hilly terrain and a mountain section.
Whether the raised strength frequency stays compatible with any added running-specific volume as the event approaches.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 143 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 7 runs)
▼ 4-week volume 128 km vs 133 km prior block (-4%)
